Test: the deal matches criteria written down before any listing was looked at: format, radius, minimum gross, maximum owner hours
ProofIs: the criteria file, dated earlier than the listing
Why: Criteria written after a listing appears are a description of that listing. The date on the file is the whole test.

Test: 12 months of the seller's own utility bills and 3 years of tax returns, and the gross they imply lands within 10 percent of the asking claim
ProofIs: the bills, the returns, and the arithmetic reconciling them to the claim
Why: Water in and quarters out are the 2 numbers a seller cannot easily dress. A claimed gross with no utility bill behind it is a number somebody typed.

Test: owner cash flow stays positive on the verified numbers after a real manager wage, real utilities, real rent and a real repair line
ProofIs: the underwriting row for this deal, built on G2 numbers only
Why: Seller's discretionary earnings usually assumes Amanda works there for free. Put the wage back in. If it only works when she is the labour, she bought a job at a premium.

Test: every machine listed with its age, and a written replacement cost for every unit past the useful life the file names
ProofIs: the machine list, and the replacement total
Why: The repair bill is the difference between this and a vending route. It arrives whether or not it was budgeted for.

Test: remaining term plus options runs longer than the loan, in writing, with the assignment clause and any exclusivity read in full
ProofIs: the lease, and the landlord's written consent to assign
Why: The machines are worth a fraction of what was paid for them the moment they have nowhere to sit. A lease shorter than the note means the landlord sets the price of year 6.

Test: cash remaining after closing clears the reserve floor written at station S14
ProofIs: the closing statement and the Fresh Spin balance the day after
Why: This is the gate that cannot be answered by the deal, only by a balance that existed before it. It is why S14 is a clock station and starts early.

Test: debt service coverage clears the ratio written in the file, computed on the G3 cash flow rather than the seller's
ProofIs: the amortisation schedule against the verified cash flow
Why: A structure that only works at the seller's numbers is a structure that works on paper. The ratio is written before the deal so the deal cannot move it.

Test: the deal still services its debt with revenue down 20 percent and 2 machines replaced inside year 1
ProofIs: the same model run at the downside numbers
Why: Nothing here predicts a downturn. It asks what happens if the ordinary bad year arrives first instead of third.
